recognize: how the picture is taken: shot size, lens, angle, film look. Words that name only one of those ("camera angle", "selfie angle", "lens") are a "list" of it, not a camera.
reader.heading: For a camera:
reader.text: vary, the parts of it that change, from: shot_size, lens, angle, film_look. When the part's words name one of them, only that one changes: "camera angle" and "selfie angle" vary angle alone, "lens" lens alone, "shot size" or "framing" shot_size alone, "film look" or "film stock" film_look alone. Only words for the whole camera ("camera", "camera work", "shot") vary all four, unless the prompt or a note settles some.

questions.needs_message: part {n}: a camera must vary some of shot_size, lens, angle, film_look

examples: "a street, ⟦camera⟧" (keep nothing; category "camera") -> "a wide shot at eye level on a 35mm lens", "a low-angle close-up on Kodak Portra 400 film", never "a 35mm film camera" or "a vintage camera": a camera part is how the picture is taken, never a camera in it
"⟦selfie camera angle⟧" (keep "selfie"; category "camera angle") -> "a high-angle selfie, phone held above her head", "a low selfie angle from chest height"
writer.whole: The whole part is "{cat}", how the picture is taken: every variant is a specific way of taking it (a shot size, an angle, a lens, a film look), never a device in the picture and never "by" or "with" one.

improve: A value that says how the picture is taken (a shot, a lens, an angle, a film stock) is never a thing in it, and alone it does not make the picture a photo: no one holds, uses or is framed by a camera because of it.
